title: Inheritance and Variation
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Inheritance and Variation Worksheets (Offspring, Genes, Selective Breeding)
standard_text: Recognise that living things produce offspring of the same kind, but normally offspring vary and are not identical to their parents.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on inheritance and variation: offspring, inherited and environmental characteristics, variation data, selective breeding and Gregor Mendel. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Like their parents, but never identical.
key_sub: Genes pass on characteristics; the environment changes others.
body_html:
How to think about it

Offspring are the same kind as their parents, but they vary.

  • Inherited characteristics (eye colour, blood group) are passed on in genes. Environmental ones (a scar, a language you learn) are not.
  • Some, such as height, depend on both genes and the environment.
  • Variation means individuals of the same species are different. People use it in selective breeding.
Example

Dyed purple hair: inherited?

It comes from a choice, not genes

Answer: No, environmental

Example

Farmers want more milk. What do they do?

Choose the best milk cows as parents

Answer: selective breeding

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a scar or a skill can be passed on to children.
  • Thinking brothers and sisters are identical.
  • Thinking variation means a different species.

faq.a: Passing characteristics, such as eye colour, from parents to offspring through genes.

faq.q: Why are offspring not identical to their parents?
faq.a: Each offspring gets a different mix of genes from its two parents, so there is variation even within one family.
Choosing parents with a wanted characteristic, such as high milk yield, and breeding them over many generations so the characteristic becomes more common.
